system_description.narrative_title: Fragile multipolar order under energy, war and market stress
system_description.narrative_summary: A multipolar, tightly interdependent global system is in flux as regional wars, energy-supply shocks and great-power rivalry produce synchronized political and market shocks. Financial markets and central banks are grappling with stronger-than-expected US data and rising yields even as conflicts (notably U.S.–Iran hostilities and the Russia–Ukraine war) and sanctions-driven adjustments disrupt oil, gas and strategic supply chains. Beijing–Washington friction and opportunistic partnerships (eg. Russia–Iran) complicate diplomacy, leaving Europe and other regions exposed to winter energy risk and political polarization at home.
system_description.scope: The global political-economic-security system: sovereign states, alliances and rivalries; energy and commodity flows; international financial markets and central banks; sanctions, trade and supply chains; multinational firms and critical technologies; multilateral institutions and regional conflicts.
system_description.super_system: The planetary socio-economic-ecological system — human civilization embedded in and dependent on global resources, trade networks, and the biosphere.
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy system (oil, gas, refining, shipping via Hormuz and trade routes)
International financial markets and central banking system (sovereign debt, yields, gold, FX)
Regional security complexes (Middle East/Gulf; Eastern Europe/Russia–Ukraine)
Global supply chains & high-tech ecosystem (chips, rare earths, satellite/space links)

variables.name: U.S.-Iran maritime confrontation
variables.description: The United States and Iran are engaged in an escalating maritime campaign of strikes, escorts and interdictions that is shifting operational norms and military posture at sea.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine high-intensity war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine remain locked in a high‑intensity war characterized by drone and missile strikes, periodic battlefield shifts and intermittent diplomatic initiatives that are reshaping security dynamics in Europe.

variables.name: Global energy market disruption
variables.description: Major oil and gas producers and consuming states are reconfiguring trade flows, inventories and refining priorities amid overlapping supply shocks and policy shifts, driving volatile markets and strategic rerouting.

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: China and the United States are contesting technology supply chains, investment and market access through export controls, tariffs and diplomatic pressure, shifting the rules and architecture of global economic competition.

variables.name: Global bond market strain and reserve rebalancing
variables.description: Central banks, sovereign treasuries and global investors are navigating a rapid repricing of interest rates and fiscal risks that is shifting capital flows, reserve management and perceptions of safe‑haven assets.
